To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) We develop a new demand model that incorporates both cross-item competitive promotion information and the cross-period effects; (2) We build a multi-period nonlinear integer programming model that maximizes category profits over a multi-period planning horizon under constraints; (3) We develop a two stage regularization approach to ensure the realistic parameters of the model; (4) Our model provides optimized prices and promotional activities together with sales and profits forecast.

(a) we develop a new model that integrates cross-SKU promotion and cross-period effects into a demand model, (b) we build a new model that optimizes prices, feature advertising and display planning, and (c) the new models outperform existing models in sales forecasts and category profits.

the proposed SKU level promotions optimization model is able to: (i) maximize category level profits over a planning period under the constraints of the business rules typically applied by retailers; (ii) deliver optimized prices, display, and feature advertising planning; (iii) generate accurate sales forecasts for all the products in a category and (iv) increase category profits by approximately17%. © 2016 Elsevier B.V.,

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we develop a model for retail category promotions optimization which is based on a new distributed lag demand model that integrates cross-SKU promotional effects and cross-period promotional influence, and that is estimated using a two stage sign constraint regularized approach.
this paper presents a novel model to help retailers optimize the promotion of individual items within a category, taking account of all the important factors that influence sales.
we have developed a model that can be used to generate a set of optimal price and promotional strategies to maximize the retailer profit over a planning horizon for a category of SKUs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed model can be used as a Decision Support System (or tool) to assist the retailers in the planning of their promotional activities.
it can provide retailers with a DSS that is capable of delivering optimized promotional decisions at SKU level.
the new model can be used to improve the retailer’s profits by optimizing the promotional schedule at the SKU level.
